$comment: Lint rules for references/amd/. Anchor grammar comes from the verified document baseline in .scratch/amd-virt-refine/spec.md §D2; every misconception below came back CONFIRMED from a primary-source check (see recheck-findings.md appendix A). Claims that were REFUTED during that check are deliberately absent — encoding them would bake in a new error.
$comment_archChapter: 01-14. Chapter 15 (nested virtualization) is deliberately outside the band: its only normative content is APM Vol.2 §15.33 and the rest is kernel and Windows Tier-2 material, so a blanket 'every claim needs a Tier-1 anchor' rule could never pass there.
$comment_claimFreeFiles: This skill has no core-facts.md: two navigation files with the same job is the seam that let the old quick-reference drift into a second fact store. 00-quickref.md navigates and holds no authoritative values.

anchors.$comment_grammar: APM section numbers carry no revision because §15.1-§15.35 have been stable since at least Rev 3.30 (2018). The revision-bearing documents embed it because their numbering moves. APM Vol.3 Ch.4 is alphabetical with page numbers only, so an instruction is cited by mnemonic — [APM3 §4.7.2 VMRUN] is a fabrication.
anchors.$comment_revguide: AMD Revision Guides are the only public AMD errata documents and are Tier-1, but the anchor table originally had no shape for them at all - a ch07 author found two real AVIC errata and correctly refused to cite them rather than invent a shape. The first version of this rule allowed section and chapter forms; that was a mistake and it immediately produced a fabricated [RevGuide 57095 section 2.1]. These documents have NO numbered sections and NO numbered chapters: the bookmark tree is Overview / Conventions / Product Errata / cross-reference tables, by title, with errata identified by number. So the only legal forms are 'erratum <n>' and 'p.<n>'. Corrected 2026-09-26: the Family 17h guides 55449 and 56323 DO cover client parts - 55449's applicable packages include AM4 and its Table 12 splits errata across Ryzen and Threadripper segments, with erratum 1235 at p.87 - so a client revision-guide citation is legal and expected. What does not exist publicly is a guide for a Family 19h or 1Ah client model range; scope a gap to that, never to 'client Ryzen has no revision guide'. See errata.md E27.
anchors.$comment_memwp: AMD memory-encryption white paper, pub 70363 (Kaplan/Powell/Woller). Added 2026-09-21: the APM does not contain the string TSME anywhere, so this paper is the only substantive source for it, and 8 of chapter 11's [no-spec] claims existed purely because no anchor shape could cite it. Second time the grammar table was found incomplete (RevGuide was the first) - a Tier-1/2 source with no citable form is a rule that cannot be satisfied honestly. Non-normative: cite by page, and never let it outrank the APM.

$comment_offSpec: Subjects the AMD manuals do not document. A Windows or CVE claim anchored only to the APM is citation filler — the section resolves, but to an unrelated subject.
$comment_unscopedNegative: Three fabricated negatives have reached this corpus. README records the first two; errata.md E27 records the third, which asserted that AMD publishes no errata channel for client parts, stood in eight places, and was refuted by this skill's own bibliography three lines below the assertion. The work contract already said a negative claim needs the same evidence as a positive one, and it did not prevent a third - so the rule is mechanical here rather than advisory. A blanket 'no such document exists' must name a publication number, carry an as-of date, or live in 90-dated-landscape.md where it is re-checked. Proved non-vacuous by injection before being committed, per README's rule that a silent rule and a broken rule look identical from the outside.

patterns.re: (there (?:is|are) no public |\b(?:AMD|Intel|Microsoft|the vendor) publishes no \b|\b(?:AMD|Intel|Microsoft) has no public \b|\bno public [a-z\- ]{0,40}(?:guide|reference|PPR|document|documentation|specification|erratum|errata|copy|source) )

unscopedNegative.message: a negative claim needs the same evidence as a positive one, scoped to a document and a date (errata.md E27)

offSpec.message: the APM does not document it

$comment_deadTitles: Empty, and that is a verified finding rather than an oversight: a bookmark-tree diff of APM Vol.2 Rev 3.30 (2018) against Rev 3.45 (2026) shows §15.1-§15.35 unchanged in number and title, and appendix letters A-E stable. AMD appends; it does not renumber. The AMD-side risk is inventing recent subsections, not citing stale ones.
$comment_legacyDocs: Pub 33047 (2005 SVM manual) and the 2007 IOMMU edition (PID 34434 Rev 1.20) may be cited for history only. In the pre-rebuild skill, 33047 alone carried 62 citations — 48 of them in the VMCB chapter, which claimed to follow the APM appendices.

legacyDocs.message: rests on a superseded AMD manual (33047 / IOMMU 34434 Rev 1.20)

$comment_misconceptions: Each entry was verified against the primary source. Deliberately NOT here: CVE-2024-25744 attribution, client-Ryzen SEV availability, CVE-2021-29657's CVSS, VMGEXIT prefix form, and the IVRS 16-byte entry class — a primary-source check refuted the 'correction' in all five cases.

misconceptions.right: CmdBufRun is a read-only bit in the IOMMU Status Register at MMIO 2020h (bit 4); the enable is CmdBufEn, Control Register 0018h bit 12
the IRTE field at bit 0 is RemapEn
the IOMMU MMIO region is 16 KiB when MMIO 0030h[PCSup]=0 and 512 KiB when PCSup=1; '14' is a misread of BaseAddress[31:14]
VMLOAD/VMSAVE transfer FS, GS, TR, LDTR, KernelGsBase, STAR/LSTAR/CSTAR/SFMASK and SYSENTER_CS/ESP/EIP — SS is not among them
the current APM states these as 'any MBZ bit of CR4/EFER is set'; the fixed masks come from the 2005 manual and would reject a legal guest state
x2AVIC is Fn8000_000A EDX[18]; EDX[14] is reserved and EDX[15] is VMSAVEvirt
the Hyper-V image on an AMD host is hvax64.exe; hvix64.exe is the Intel build

wrong.re: \b16\s*(memory references|次内存访问|次访存|次查表)

misconceptions.right: the worst-case two-dimensional walk is 24 references (nm+n+m) — and it must be cited to the AMD-V Nested Paging white paper §4.2.2 or ASPLOS'08, never to the APM, which states no such figure
exit codes are segmented (CR reads 00h-0Fh, exceptions 40h-5Fh, intercept vector 3 at 0x60+bit, vector 4 at 0x80+bit), so VMRUN is 80h — not the bit's position in the vector
CVE-2022-23816 is REJECTED at NVD (vulnStatus Rejected, 'unused by its CNA'); the citable Branch Type Confusion / RETbleed identifier is CVE-2022-29900

$comment_correctionHints: Chinese negations are included because every chapter opens with a 中文速览 that frequently states the correction — e.g. 「不含 SS」 — and would otherwise trip the very rule it is obeying.

correctionHints.re: \bnever\b|\bdoes not\b|\bnot among\b|\bnot include\b|refuted|\bnot\b.{0,20}(CVE-|AMD-SB-|Rev)|已作废|口径已更正|不含|不包括|并非|而不是|不在其中|rejected (at|by) nvd|\bhas since rejected\b|unused by its cna|the citable (identifier|id)|\bsuperseded\b|\bwithdrawn\b
correctionHints.$note: Phrases are deliberately narrow, not single broad words. A line that NAMES a misconception in order to correct it must not be flagged - the corpus has to be able to quote a wrong claim to refute it, the same principle eval/RUNNER.md states as 'a refutation is not a violation'. But a hint like a bare 'rejected' would exempt any line containing it, including one that genuinely asserts the misconception, so each addition is a phrase specific to the correction it unblocks.

ownership.$comment: The escape clause accepts only an explicit `NN-file.md` cross-reference. A bare 'see' silenced 71 of 73 hits in the Intel subtree, which made the whole rule a no-op.

rules.$note: Boundary: 08 owns the GA log as a DATA STRUCTURE (entry format, the registers that size and point at it, full/empty arithmetic, overflow, restart); 10 owns it as a SIGNAL (why an entry is written, what GATag means, GAPPI as the alternative). The token list is register and entry-type names only. It deliberately excludes GALogIntr, which is an IRTE field and belongs to 10 - an earlier broader  GALog[A-Za-z]+  caught it and was a false positive.
GA log moved to 08: it owns the event and PPR log entry formats, and one of three log formats living elsewhere is a hairline split that drifts. 10 keeps GA log semantics and cross-references 08.

terminology.right: the IRTE bit-0 field is RemapEn
VIRT_EXT is the Linux/KVM name; AMD calls it VMCB offset 0B8h
AMD's term is system physical address (sPA)
SEV_STATUS bit 7 is DebugVirtualization in AMD's table; 'Debug Swap' is the Linux name

$comment_orphanExemptBelow: IDs 1-40 are the preloaded AMD specification set and 41-99 the other official specifications; both may sit uncited.
$comment_terminology_quickref: 00-quickref.md is exempt from the terminology rules because its section 0.4 is a wrong-name to AMD-name mapping table - naming the wrong term is the whole function of that section, exactly as errata.md must quote a misconception to correct it. The exemption is scoped to terminology ONLY: quickref is still subject to the misconception rules, still forbidden from carrying claim lines (claimFreeFiles), and still holds no authoritative values, so it cannot become a second fact store the way the old appendix did.
